svg.text: EnergyHub — Who May Control What?
Separate authorities cooperate; a legacy class or MQTT name is not a new control owner
EH → INVERTER
Reserve/night/pre-outage policies request modes
InverterController executes verified commands
Durable transition marker before hardware writes
ACK + Menu 01 readback; Menu 16 is ACK-only
NATIVE HA → SMART PLUGS
Overload: five configured plug roles
Battery preservation: four plugs + separate fridge
Shared saved-state/interlock helpers coordinate OFF
Python no longer dispatches plug shed/restore
EH + HA → FIRST-FLOOR HP
EH owns HP1 battery policy and restart context
HA bridge executes allowed climate actions
HA also owns schedule/profile helper automations
HP1 relay is excluded from native plug shedding
FAMILY AUTHORITY · different paths
HP1 family OFF/manual hold blocks optional restart
Native plugs OFF before a cycle remain OFF
A newer OFF during a native saved cycle is not
a tracked cancellation of its saved ON intention
EVIDENCE · path-specific guarantees
Freshness, grid agreement and SOC gates apply
HP commands require acknowledgements/context
Native plug notices describe commands sent
They are not physical-switching confirmations
FAILURES · do not invent success
Missing data does not mean a safe ON condition
Uncertain inverter state needs attended review
No blanket auto-reboot or hardware reset
Compatibility IDs/journals remain deliberately
Native plug restoration can override a later family OFF inside a saved cycle. Do not claim universal manual-OFF protection.
